[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **brackets** and **multiplication** first: (39 + 16) × 2 = 55 × 2 = 110.

Combine all **positive** numbers: 49 + 86 + 110 = 245.

Combine all **negative** numbers: 58 + 47 = 105.

Final result: 245 − 105 = 140.

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 49 + 86 − 58 + (39 + 16) × 2 − 47

Applying the **BODMAS** rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 49 + 86 − 58 + (55) × 2 − 47

⇒ 49 + 86 − 58 + 110 − 47

⇒ 135 − 58 + 110 − 47

⇒ 77 + 110 − 47

⇒ 187 − 47

⇒ 140

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It ensures calculations are performed in a fixed order: **Brackets** (), **Of**, **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Sign Convention in Addition

When adding or subtracting, group terms with the same sign to simplify the operation: (Sum of positives) − (Sum of negatives).

Multiplication Priority

Always complete **multiplication** and **division** before performing addition and subtraction unless brackets dictate otherwise.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS** by grouping positive and negative terms for faster calculation.

Expression: 88 + 26 − 19 + 37 + 32 − 28 + 14

Positive terms: (88 + 32) + (26 + 14) + 37 ⇒ 120 + 40 + 37 = 197

Negative terms: 19 + 28 = 47

Final Value: 197 − 47 = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 88 + 26 − (19 × 1) + 37 ÷ 1 + 32 − 28 + 14

Follow the **BODMAS** rule to solve the operations in order:

⇒ 88 + 26 − 19 + 37 ÷ 1 + 32 − 28 + 14 (Solving **Bracket** 19 × 1)

⇒ 88 + 26 − 19 + 37 + 32 − 28 + 14 (Solving **Division** 37 ÷ 1)

⇒ 114 − 19 + 37 + 32 − 28 + 14 (Performing **Addition**: 88 + 26)

⇒ 95 + 37 + 32 − 28 + 14 (Performing **Subtraction**: 114 − 19)

⇒ 132 + 32 − 28 + 14 (Performing **Addition**: 95 + 37)

⇒ 164 − 28 + 14 (Performing **Addition**: 132 + 32)

⇒ 136 + 14 (Performing **Subtraction**: 164 − 28)

⇒ 150 (Final **Addition**)

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The acronym stands for **Bracket**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**. It dictates the priority of operations in mathematics to ensure a unique result.

Simplification Tips

Always check for numbers that form **round figures** (like 88 + 32 = 120 or 26 + 14 = 40) to simplify manual addition and reduce calculation errors.

questions.question: A and B can finish the work in 10 days and 15 days, respectively. They start working together. After 3 days, A leaves. How many days will B take to finish the remaining work? What is the total number of days taken to complete the entire work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 3 and Efficiency of **B** = 2.

Work done together in 3 days = (3 + 2) × 3 = 15 units.

Remaining work = 30 − 15 = 15 units.

Days for B to finish remaining = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 days; Total days = 3 + 7.5 = 10.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 days; 10.5 days.**

questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Convert all ratios to **milk fractions**: Mix 1 = 3/4, Mix 2 = 5/8, and Resultant = 4/6 = 2/3. Apply **Alligation** on milk concentration: Left side (Mix 1 − Mean): 3/4 − 2/3 = (9 − 8)/12 = 1/12 Right side (Mean − Mix 2): 2/3 − 5/8 = (16 − 15)/24 = 1/24 Required Ratio = (1/24) : (1/12) = 1 : 2. **∴ The correct answer is 1:2.**

questions.question: A group of 8 pumps can fill a tank in 15 hours. After working for 5 hours, 4 more pumps are added. Find the total time required to fill the tank.
questions.solution:

Work remaining after 5 hours = 8 pumps × 10 hours = 80 pump-hours.

New number of pumps = 8 + 4 = 12 pumps.

Additional time needed = Remaining work ÷ Total pumps = 80 ÷ 12 = 6.67 hr.

**Total time** required = Initial time + Additional time = 5 + 6.67 = 11.67 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.67 hr.**

questions.question:
Arrange the following values in descending order.

4(1)/(3), (14)/(3), 4(1)/(2), (29)/(6)
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Convert each fraction into its **decimal** equivalent to compare values directly. 4(1/3) = 13 ÷ 3 ≈ 4.333 14/3 = 14 ÷ 3 ≈ 4.667 4(1/2) = 4.500 29/6 = 29 ÷ 6 ≈ 4.833 Comparing the values: 4.833 > 4.667 > 4.500 > 4.333 **∴ The correct answer is 29/6 > 14/3 > 4(1/2) > 4(1/3).**

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 9177. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Estimate the **middle number** by calculating the **cube root** of the product: ³√9177 ≈ 20.94.

Identify the **consecutive odd numbers** near 21, which are 19, 21, and 23.

Verify the **unit digit** product: 9 × 1 × 3 = 27 (Last digit 7 matches 9177).

The **largest number** among 19, 21, and 23 is 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of **three consecutive odd numbers** = 9177.

**Formula Used:**

If the **middle number** is x, then the numbers are (x − 2), x, and (x + 2).

Product = (x − 2) × x × (x + 2) = x × (x² − 4) = x³ − 4x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab0436b7b6062226a0303da1572c489a538c973c3c0ff9294385b2e2680c250d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x³ − 4x = 9177

⇒ We know that 20³ = 8000 and 22³ = 10648.

⇒ Testing **odd number** x = 21:

⇒ 21³ − 4(21) = 9261 − 84 = 9177 (Matches given product).

⇒ The numbers are 19, 21, and 23.

⇒ The **largest** of these numbers is 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression of Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a **common difference (d)** of 2. They can be represented as n, n+2, n+4...

Average of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The **average** of an odd number of consecutive terms in an AP is always the middle term.

Properties of Odd Products

The product of any number of odd integers is **always odd**. If the product is even, at least one of the numbers must be even.

Eliminate **multiples**: 121 (11×11), 123 (3×41), 125 (5×25), 129 (3×43), 133 (7×19), 135 (5×27).

The remaining **prime numbers** are: 127, 131, 137, and 139.

Sum = 127 + 131 + 137 + 139 = 534.

**∴ The correct answer is 534.**

questions.question: (380 + 120)² - (380 - 120)² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity: **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab**.

Here, let **a = 380** and **b = 120**.

Expression = 4 × 380 × 120.

Split the factor 4 into 2 × 2 ⇒ (2 × 380) × (2 × 120) = **760 × 240**.

**∴ The correct answer is 760 × 240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (380 + 120)² − (380 − 120)²

**Formula Used:** X² − Y² = (X + Y)(X − Y)

⇒ Let **X = (380 + 120)** and **Y = (380 − 120)**.

⇒ Expression = [(380 + 120) + (380 − 120)] × [(380 + 120) − (380 − 120)]

⇒ Expression = [380 + 120 + 380 − 120] × [380 + 120 − 380 + 120]

⇒ Expression = [2 × 380] × [2 × 120]

⇒ Expression = 760 × 240

**∴ The correct answer is 760 × 240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity - Sum Case

When the squares are added, the identity becomes: **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)**.

Standard Squaring Formulas

The expansion **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** and **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²** are fundamental for solving quadratic and simplification problems.

Difference of Two Squares

The rule **a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)** is used to factorize expressions or simplify products of large numbers.

questions.question: A square park has sides of length 10 cm. A 2 cm wide path is inside it. What is the area (in square cm) of the path?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The area of a **path inside a square** is calculated as: 4w(S − w) Given **side (S)** = 10 cm and **path width (w)** = 2 cm. Area = 4 × 2 × (10 − 2) Area = 8 × 8 = 64 cm². **∴ The correct answer is 64 cm².**

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle is 5 cm and 7 cm respectively. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Area of a Rectangle** is the product of its **Length** and **Breadth**.

**Area** = 5 × 7 = 35 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 35 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the rectangle (L) = 5 cm

**Breadth** of the rectangle (B) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of a **Rectangle** = **Length** × **Breadth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed4c23906a91ed7282ef7a9238ea6dccf813b210bfa12ebba2072cb2dedc4f5a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Area** = 5 cm × 7 cm

⇒ **Area** = 35 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 35 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the boundary of a rectangle is P = 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The straight line connecting opposite vertices is calculated using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(L² + B²).

Area of a Square

For a square, where Length = Breadth = side (a), the **Area** = a² and **Perimeter** = 4a.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. The length of the rectangle is 12 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Semi-perimeter (l + b) = **Perimeter** ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm.

**Breadth** (b) = Semi-perimeter − **Length** = 20 − 12 = 8 cm.

**Area** = Length × Breadth = 12 × 8 = 96 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the rectangle = 40 cm

**Length** (l) of the rectangle = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Area** = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/237152317a9579bab26b390ae7971a59e0092222547dee7bdd44a396d1aff0f1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (12 + Breadth) = 40

⇒ 12 + Breadth = 40 ÷ 2

⇒ 12 + Breadth = 20

⇒ **Breadth** = 20 − 12 = 8 cm

⇒ **Area** = 12 × 8

⇒ **Area** = 96 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite vertices, calculated as d = √(l² + b²).

Area of a Square

A square is a special rectangle where length = breadth; Area = side × side = a².

Perimeter vs Area Units

Perimeter is a 1D measure (cm, m), while Area is a 2D measure (cm², m²).

questions.question: 21² + 22² + 23² + ...... + 50² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required **sum of squares** is calculated by subtracting the sum of the first 20 squares from the sum of the first 50 squares.

Formula for **sum of squares** of first n natural numbers = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

Sum (1 to 50) = (50 × 51 × 101) ÷ 6 = 42925.

Sum (1 to 20) = (20 × 21 × 41) ÷ 6 = 2870.

Required Sum = 42925 − 2870 = 40055.

**∴ The correct answer is 40055.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Series: 21² + 22² + 23² + ...... + 50².

**Formula Used:**

The sum of the squares of the first n **natural numbers** (Σn²) is given by: [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Required Sum = (1² + 2² + ... + 50²) − (1² + 2² + ... + 20²)

⇒ Sum = Σ₁⁵⁰ n² − Σ₁²⁰ n²

⇒ Sum = [50 × (50 + 1) × (2 × 50 + 1) ÷ 6] − [20 × (20 + 1) × (2 × 20 + 1) ÷ 6]

⇒ Sum = [50 × 51 × 101 ÷ 6] − [20 × 21 × 41 ÷ 6]

⇒ Sum = (25 × 17 × 101) − (10 × 7 × 41)

⇒ Sum = 42925 − 2870

⇒ Sum = 40055.

**∴ The correct answer is 40055.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum is calculated as [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Sum of Cubes of First n Natural Numbers

The sum is the square of the sum of the first n natural numbers: [{n(n + 1)} ÷ 2]².

Sum of First n Even Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive even natural numbers is given by n(n + 1).

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd natural numbers is given by n².

questions.question: The average expenditure of R for 5 days is Rs. 150. His expenditure for the first 4 days is Rs. 100, Rs. 155, Rs. 70 and Rs. 200 respectively. What is his expenditure (in Rs.) on the 5th day?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Assume the **Average** as 150. Calculate the **Net Deviation** of the first 4 days from this average. **Net Deviation** = (100 − 150) + (155 − 150) + (70 − 150) + (200 − 150) ⇒ −50 + 5 − 80 + 50 = −75. To maintain the **Average** of 150, the 5th day expenditure must compensate for this deficit. ⇒ 5th Day Expenditure = 150 + 75 = 225. **∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

questions.question: Average age of 12 boys is 15 years. Average age of 8 girls is 10 years. What is the combined average age (in years) of these boys and girls?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 12 : 8 = **3 : 2**

Using **Weighted Average** ratio method:

Combined Average = (Ratio₁ × Avg₁ + Ratio₂ × Avg₂) ÷ (Total Ratio)

= (3 × 15 + 2 × 10) ÷ (3 + 2) = (45 + 20) ÷ 5 = 65 ÷ 5 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

questions.question: Which number is 30 percent less than 60 percent of 800?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct multiplication method: **Result** = **Base** × **60%** × (100% − **30%**)

Result = 800 × 0.60 × 0.70

Result = 800 × 0.42 = 336

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Base number = 800, Step 1 = 60% of base, Step 2 = 30% reduction of Step 1 result.

**Formula Used:** Value = (Percentage/100) × Number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a6394c4149ae0eee65f5c8ab9e5f03d98ace50c0de4b9d3fe772c0e85057c25.png] 

⇒ First, calculate 60% of 800:

⇒ 60% of 800 = (60 ÷ 100) × 800 = 0.6 × 800 = 480

⇒ Now, find the number which is 30% less than 480:

⇒ Required number = 480 − (30% of 480)

⇒ Required number = 480 − (0.3 × 480) = 480 − 144

⇒ Required number = 336

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Decrease Formula

To find a value x% less than y, use the formula: New Value = y × (1 − x/100).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a × b)/100]%. For decreases, use negative values.

Decimal Conversion

Always convert percentages to decimals for faster manual calculation (e.g., 60% = 0.6, 30% = 0.3).

questions.question: Cost price of 25 articles is Rs. 197. Selling price of 30 articles is Rs. 197. What is the ratio of the value of profit/loss of 1 article to the selling price of 1 article? (Cost price of all the articles is same. Selling price of all the articles is same.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **Cost Price (CP)** of x articles = **Selling Price (SP)** of y articles, then CP/SP = y/x.

Given: CP × 25 = SP × 30 ⇒ CP/SP = 30/25 = 6/5.

Let CP = 6 units and SP = 5 units. Since CP > SP, there is a **Loss**.

**Loss** = CP − SP = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

Required **Ratio** = Loss : SP = 1 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.**

questions.question: A pipe can empty a tank in 36 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) it can empty 1/4 part of this tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to empty 1 full tank = 36 min.

To empty 1/4th of the tank, the time required will be 1/4th of the **total time**.

Required time = 36 × 1/4 = 9 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total time to empty the tank = 36 min.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity (units)**
 **Efficiency (units/min)**
 
 

 Pipe A
 36
 36
 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total capacity of the tank be 36 units (LCM of 36).

⇒ **Efficiency** of the pipe = Total Capacity ÷ Total Time

⇒ Efficiency = 36 ÷ 36 = 1 unit/min (emptying rate).

⇒ Capacity to be emptied = 1/4 × 36 = 9 units.

⇒ Time taken = Capacity to be emptied ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 9 ÷ 1 = 9 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part filled in 1 hour = 1/x. Similarly, if an outlet pipe empties it in y hours, the part emptied in 1 hour = 1/y.

Work and Time Relation

Work Done = Rate × Time. For a constant rate, the time taken is directly proportional to the amount of work (or volume) to be completed.

Fractional Work

To find the time for a fraction of work '1/n', simply multiply the total time by the fraction '1/n'.

questions.question: R1 alone can do a work in 18 days working 6 hours a day. R2 alone can do the same work in 12 days working 9 hours per day. Working 6 hours per day, in how many days both R1 and R2 together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total hours for **R1** = 18 days × 6 hr/day = 108 hr.

Total hours for **R2** = 12 days × 9 hr/day = 108 hr.

Both take equal total hours, so their efficiency is the same.

Combined time = 108 ÷ 2 = 54 hours.

Number of days at 6 hr/day = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

questions.question: The sum of 6 percent of first number and 4 percent of second number is 2 times of the sum of 2 percent of first number and 5 percent of second number. What is the ratio of first number to the second number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the **percentage coefficients** directly by removing the common denominator 100.

LHS: 6 × 1st + 4 × 2ⁿd | RHS: 2 × (2 × 1st + 5 × 2ⁿd) = 4 × 1st + 10 × 2ⁿd.

Balance the 1st number: 6 − 4 = 2 parts.

Balance the 2ⁿd number: 10 − 4 = 6 parts.

2 × **First Number** = 6 × **Second Number** ⇒ Ratio = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the **first number** be x and the **second number** be y.

**Formula Used:**

The percentage of a number is given by (Rate/100) × Number. Ratio is the comparison of two quantities x : y.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d21506cb770fe75666ab9cefd0c6c1e10de3638feb3135d133a3896a8a8feaff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (6/100)x + (4/100)y = 2 × [(2/100)x + (5/100)y]

⇒ 6x + 4y = 2(2x + 5y)

⇒ 6x + 4y = 4x + 10y

⇒ 6x − 4x = 10y − 4y

⇒ 2x = 6y

⇒ x/y = 6/2

⇒ x/y = 3/1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion Basics

A **ratio** compares two quantities. If a : b = c : d, then a × d = b × c (Product of extremes = Product of means).

Linear Equation Solving

To solve for ratios in **linear equations**, group all terms containing the first variable on one side and the second variable on the other.

Percentage Simplification

When every term in an algebraic equation contains a **percentage**, the 1/100 factor can be cancelled out from all terms simultaneously to work with integers.
